title: DDR (Double Data Rate) memory timing
summary: DDR memory timing parameters define the timing of memory operations. Key parameters: CAS latency (CL, column address strobe), RAS to CAS delay (tRCD), Row Precharge time (tRP), Row Active time (tRAS), Row Cycle time (tRC = tRAS + tRP). DDR transfers data on both clock edges (rising and falling), doubling bandwidth. DDR4: 2133-3200 MT/s. DDR5: 4800-8400 MT/s.

structure.meaning: Column Address Strobe latency: time from column address to data available. E.g., CL16 = 16 cycles.
Time from row activation to column access. Typically equal to CL.
Time to precharge (close) a row before opening a new one. Typically equal to CL.
Minimum time a row must be active. tRAS = tRCD + tCAS + tBURST (typically 30-40 cycles).
tRC = tRAS + tRP. Minimum time between row activations.
Data transferred on both rising and falling clock edges. 2x bandwidth vs SDR.
8 data beats per access (BL8). Each beat = 64 bits (8 bytes). Total = 64 bytes = cache line size.
DDR4: 8n prefetch (8 beats fetched per access). DDR5: 16n prefetch (16 beats).

notes: DDR5 has two 32-bit channels per DIMM (vs DDR4's single 64-bit channel).
Memory latency = CL / (frequency/2) in nanoseconds. E.g., CL16 @ 3200 MT/s = 16 / 1600 = 10ns.
Row buffer (page) hit: ~10ns. Row miss: ~30ns (activate + read).
DDR is the main memory in virtually all computers.
